neighbours.label: a scientific law, theorem or theory as the source that states a claim (the law states / the theorem shows that / theory tells us)
fire: In physics class we learned that Hooke's law states that stretch is proportional to load.
Put simply, the second law of thermodynamics says that entropy never decreases.
In statistics, Bayes' theorem tells us how to update a belief given new evidence.
As a rule, game theory predicts that rational players will defect in a single round.
Long ago, Kepler's third law showed that orbital period depends on distance.
In chemistry, Boyle's law states that pressure rises as volume shrinks.
Here the Pythagorean theorem shows that the diagonal is five units long.
In biology, cell theory holds that all living things are made of cells.
quiet: In physics class we learned that the bell rings at ten past three.
Put simply, the instruction manual says that the lid never comes off.
In statistics class, our teacher tells us how to update the spreadsheet.
As a rule, the coach predicts that tired players will slow down late.
Long ago, the town map showed that the river ran past the mill.
In chemistry, the lab notice states that goggles must be worn.
Here the receipt shows that the total was five pounds.
In biology, our textbook cover shows a frog on a lily pad.
